Bitwarden review: digital legacy verdict

Verdict: The best-value password manager with real emergency access: trusted contacts can request View or Takeover access after a wait time you set. Best for: Budget-conscious people who want a proper, tested emergency-access workflow.

Key facts

  • Category: Vaults & password managers
  • Pricing: Free plan available; Emergency Access requires Premium or a paid Families/Teams/Enterprise plan. Check current pricing.
  • Best for: Budget-conscious people who want a proper, tested emergency-access workflow.
  • Emergency contacts only need a free Bitwarden account
  • Choose View-only or Takeover access with a custom wait time

Official site / docs ↗

What are the pros and cons of Bitwarden?

Pros

  • Emergency contacts only need a free Bitwarden account
  • Choose View-only or Takeover access with a custom wait time
  • Open-source and independently audited
  • No limit on the number of emergency contacts

Cons

  • Contact must be on the same Bitwarden server region (US/EU)
  • Can't add or edit contacts if Premium lapses (existing ones still work)
  • Interface is functional rather than polished

What are similar tools?

Vaults & password managers

1Password

Excellent password manager, but it has no automatic emergency-access feature. Legacy planning relies on the Emergency Kit and family account recovery.

Vaults & password managers

Keeper

A solid choice with built-in Emergency Access: name trusted contacts who can request your vault after a wait period.

Vaults & password managers

LastPass Emergency Access

It works: contacts can request vault access after a wait period. LastPass's 2022 security breaches are a good reason to look at alternatives first, though.
